chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar quoted Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abi Umayr, on the authority of Aban ibn Uthman, on the authority of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

He said: A man came to him and said to him, 'O may my father and mother be your ransom, advise me with an advice.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'If God, the Blessed and Exalted, has guaranteed the provision, then why is your concern? And if the provision is apportioned, then why is your greed? And if the Reckoning is true, then why is your gathering [of wealth]? And if the succession [of wealth to heirs] from God is true, then why is your miserliness? And if the punishment of the Fire is [true], then why is your sinning? And if death is true, then why is your happiness [in worldly life]? And if the presentation [of deeds] before God is true, then why is your cunning? And if the passage over the Bridge is true, then why is your self-delusion? And if everything is by Divine Decree and Destiny, then why is your sorrow? And if this world is ephemeral, then why is your reliance upon it?'
ai.seo_question: What are the ten logical reflections on faith and worldly behavior taught by Imam al-Sadiq in this hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal*, this hadith presents a cohesive theological argument where Imam al-Sadiq (AS) dismantles human anxiety by linking emotional states to their underlying beliefs in divine decree (*Qadr*) and provision (*Rizq*). The scholar highlights how this rhetorical structure serves as a practical guide for *Tawakkul*, urging believers to align their inner peace with the certainty of the Hereafter and the transient nature of the world.
